It only requires the generic `json_t` dispatch to take the bool arm on leading `'f'` and this 4-byte guard to pass with `end - it == 4`, which is exactly what the staged witness and stack establish before the unsafe memcpy executes.

Source. This is the first project statement that turns the witness bytes into the `it..end` state consumed by the JSON parser; the missing bound check later depends on the fact that only four bytes are in-range from `it` to `end`.

On the witnessed path, the preceding guard only established `end - it >= 4`, and the `Opts.null_terminated` branch omitted any `end - it >= 5` check before this memcpy. The staged patch fixes that exact obligation by reading four bytes first and explicitly rejecting `false` when `it == end` before probing the fifth byte.
